newsitem.title: UK: Euro vegetable oils end quiet session little changed.
newsitem.headline: Euro vegetable oils end quiet session little changed.

text.p: Closing European vegetable oil prices were little changed on Friday as business fizzled out ahead of the weekend.

Volatile Chicago futures subdued trading with soybeans surging again on concern over supplies while lower than expected old crop soyoil exports during the week ending May 22 weighed on soy oil futures.
The USDA put old crop soy oil exports at 800 tonnes for the week ending May 22 against U.S. trade expectations of 4,000 to 6,000 tonnes.
Traders in Europe said they were not concerned by the reports of tight supplies of soybeans as 90 percent of beans crushed in Europe came from South America.
Also at this time of year all beans going to the mills are of south American origin, they added.
"It's only taking three days to load soybeans in South American ports at the moment so we have no problems," said one trader.
At the close Dutch soy oil was 0.50 guilders up after Aug/Oct traded at 105 guilders while rape oil was unchanged to 0.50 guilders down after Aug/Oct fetched 104.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Palm oil was quiet ahead of fresh Malaysian export data due next week.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed unchanged while RBD palm oil was $2.50 lower.
Palm olein closed $5 to $2.50 lower with no further business reported.
Lauric oils were neglected and closed with coconut oil $5 up to $2.50 down while palmkernel oil was unchanged to $2.50 down.
